rv.q: Now here he is, more than three decades later, still dancing – out of frustration, defiance, resistance and a desire to connect. As the percussive score gains momentum, Rajeh’s busy body builds up a sweat. In this danced stream of consciousness, Rajeh is not always an especially elegant mover, but he dances like it’s a necessary thing to do.

Rajeh is a big player in the Arab dance world having founded Maqamat in 2002, a "pioneering contemporary dance organisation". Due to political unrest and the Beirut Port explosion in 2020, Rajeh and Maqamat relocated to Lyon, France. In practical terms I assume the relocation was welcomed, but emotionally I imagine the work is ongoing.
